new_explicit_records.rationale: External-writer ring-buffer ownership/metadata/callback API belongs to the positively identified ARM protected-hypervisor tracing integration: arch/arm64/kvm/hyp_trace.c constructs the writer and invokes reader/poll helpers. That architecture backend is outside the current x86 SDK target. Keep native buffer ownership, allocation signature and read/mmap algorithms; the independent Android page-size default is now adapted. This does not assert that no unknown external consumer could ever use a general writer API. This replaces the stale whole-file-native witness with a scoped preservation proof; no new runtime validation.

Public buffer_data_page layout and timestamp/alignment material support the same external protected-hypervisor writer. Keep native internal definitions and supported ordinary trace interfaces; no shared externally produced buffer is added solely for the excluded ARM target. Native and emulated-page SDK trace readers remain supported. Future module consumers of the exposed material are not claimed absent. This replaces the stale whole-file-native witness with a scoped preservation proof; no new runtime validation.

Correction removes invalid fast-path pointer arithmetic in rb_page_desc, which is part of the excluded external-writer implementation. The helper is absent with that feature; the faulty arithmetic is not retained anywhere. No native descriptor path is replaced. This replaces the stale whole-file-native witness with a scoped preservation proof; no new runtime validation.

External writer reset/read-stamp/id/empty-buffer corrections apply to the excluded writer callback path. Preserve native owned-reader reset and timestamp algorithms, with no implementation of the old faulty external writer. SDK page-size default is independent. This replaces the stale whole-file-native witness with a scoped preservation proof; no new runtime validation.

External writer fast-forward handling and CONFIG_PKVM_DUMP_TRACE_ON_PANIC warning relaxation are coupled to ARM hypervisor trace shared metadata. That backend is outside x86 SDK scope; retain native ordinary-reader validation without importing the external-writer path or suppressing native warnings. This replaces the stale whole-file-native witness with a scoped preservation proof; no new runtime validation.

Native 27d7fcaf237d supplies alloc_cpu_buffer/page/data helpers, NUMA placement and initialization/error behavior. Whole ring_buffer.c, including all helper/caller bodies, remains LTS except the separately tested emulated allocation default. No older helper implementation is imported. This replaces the stale whole-file-native witness with a scoped preservation proof; no new runtime validation.

Native 50f4a793c4ff supplies page-capacity-based sizing and reader/resize locking correction. Preserve all native bodies and later LTS fixes, including resize_disabled before order publication and persistent buffer validation. ACK external-writer-specific conditions are inapplicable with the excluded backend; native resize fixes are fully retained. This replaces the stale whole-file-native witness with a scoped preservation proof; no new runtime validation.

native_preservation: Whole native ring_buffer.c restored by normalizing only new emulated allocation default/header/comment; public ring_buffer.h exactly native. Full seven patches reread.
